extracted.intended_audience: International Preliminary Examining Authorities, receiving Offices, and patent applicants/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for processing a PCT demand (Form PCT/IPEA/401 etc.) by an International Preliminary Examining Authority, including checks on timeliness, particulars, signatures, language, fees, transmission and excuse-of-delay rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of demand constitutes election of Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a demand constitutes the election of all Contracting States which are ... (reference to Article 37; Rule 53.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the demand is the act by which the applicant elects the Contracting States for international preliminary examination; see Article 37 and Rule 53.7 for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check of particulars affecting date of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, after checking of particulars affecting the date of receipt, a positive determination is made, the actual filing date is marked as date of receipt on the first sheet of the demand. If the demand Form or a compliant computer print-out was not used, the correction procedure in paragraphs 22.24 et seq. applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark actual filing date on first sheet (demand). If wrong form used, follow defect-correction procedures (see paragraphs 22.24 et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of receipt to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Examining Authority notifies the applicant of the receipt of the demand (Form PCT/IPEA/402).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PCT/IPEA/402 to notify applicant of receipt and date of actual receipt; notify promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness check of demand (three months/22 months rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority checks that the demand is filed within three months from transmittal of the international search report or declaration referred to in Article 17(2)(a), and the written opinion under Rule 43bis.1, or within 22 months from the priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If demand filed later, consider it not submitted and issue declaration (Form PCT/IPEA/407). If timely, notify applicant (Form PCT/IPEA/402).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special 19‑month check for States incompatible with Article 22(1) modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the national law of any designated State remains incompatible with the modification of the time limit for national phase entry under Article 22(1) (effective April 1, 2002) and such State is designated, the Authority checks whether the demand was received within 19 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If received after 19 months, mark appropriate check box on last page of demand and notify applicant and International Bureau (Form PCT/IPEA/402) promptly so applicant can enter national phase where modification is in force; irrespective of 19‑month check, notify applicant of date of actual receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing the IPEA file promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the demand, the International Preliminary Examining Authority promptly establishes the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and maintain the IPEA file immediately upon reception of the demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of same file when IPEA and ISA are same office
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IPEA is part of the same national Office or intergovernmental organization as the ISA, the same file serves both international search and international preliminary examination purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid duplicate files when possible; use the existing international search file for preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of international application and search report when IPEA is different
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA is not the same Office as the ISA or receiving Office, the International Bureau will provide a copy of the international application or the published application, together with a copy of the international search report when available, to the IPEA upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB will also forward the written opinion of the ISA upon receipt of the demand or upon request; documents cited in the search report may be obtained from IPEA's own files or ordered from the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of Article 19 amendments to IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any amendments under Article 19 and of any accompanying statement will be supplied by the International Bureau to the IPEA unless a copy has been submitted with the demand by the applicant or the applicant has reversed them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 18.04 and 18.06 for reversal and submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of demand to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA either transmits the original demand and keeps a copy in its files or sends a copy to the IB and keeps the demand in its files; the demand or copy must be transmitted to the IB even where withdrawn, considered withdrawn, or where applicant did not respond to invitation to indicate competent Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transmitted under Rule 59.3, the Authority competent to receive the demand proceeds with transmittal; ensure timely transmittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt transmittal timing (generally within one month)
rubrics_metrics.description: The transmittal must be effected promptly after receipt, generally not later than one month after receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send original or copy and any applicable powers of attorney promptly to the IB within this timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of powers of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA normally sends to the IB, together with the original demand or copy, any original separate power of attorney or any copy of a general power of attorney received; if IPEA waived POA requirement but a POA is nevertheless submitted, sending to IB is not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 90.4 and 90.5 and Section 608 for handling of POAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA should not transmit Article 34/Article 19 amendments with the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA does not transmit with the demand to the IB any amendments to the application under Article 34 or copies of amendments under Article 19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include these amendments when sending the demand to the IB (Article 34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist of certain defects in the demand (Rule 60.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA checks the demand for defects including: (i) not on prescribed Form; (ii) not signed as required; (iii) lacks prescribed indications concerning the applicant; (iv) lacks prescribed indications concerning the international application; (v) lacks prescribed indications concerning the agent; (vi) lacks petition requesting international preliminary examination (preferred words indicated but not essential); (vii) not in language of publication or language accepted by the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PCT/IPEA/404 for listing defects; see cross-references to Article 31(3), Rules 53, 55, 60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex officios corrections of certain defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Many kinds of errors in the demand can be corrected ex officio by the IPEA (applicant need not be invited). Corrections are marked with letters 'IPEA' in margin; deletions are placed in square brackets but left legible. Applicant is informed of corrections by sending a copy of corrected sheet or separate notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors that may be corrected ex officio include indications concerning the applicant and the agent; if corrected after transmittal to IB, send copy of corrected sheet to IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of incorrect check‑box markings in Box IV
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in marking check boxes in Box IV (postponement of start of examination) may be deleted ex officio by the IPEA if inconsistent with applicability of Rule 69.1(b); before making such a correction the IPEA may contact the applicant for confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delete incorrect markings; optionally confirm with applicant prior to correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement for carrying out international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where neither the language of filing nor the language of publication is accepted by the IPEA, the applicant must furnish with the demand a translation of the international application into a language accepted by the IPEA and which is a language of publication. The translation must include elements referred to in Article 11(1)(iii)(d) or (e) and any relevant parts of description, claims or drawings considered to be contained under Rule 20.6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation already furnished to the ISA and IPEA is part of same office, that translation may be used unless applicant furnishes another. IB will translate the ISA written opinion into English on request, to be forwarded within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature / power of attorney requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as set forth in paragraph 22.30, the applicant must either sign the demand or submit a separate power of attorney or copy of a signed general power of attorney appointing an agent. If two or more applicants, signature of one is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agent signs and a POA has been filed earlier with receiving Office/ISA/IB or agent appointed in the request, no POA need be submitted to the IPEA. See paragraphs 22.28–22.31 and Rules 53.2(b), 60.1(a-ter), 90.3, 90.4(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of separate power of attorney by IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA may waive the requirement that a separate power of attorney or copy of general power of attorney be submitted to it. This waiver cannot cover submission of a notice of withdrawal by an agent or common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where waiver applies, an agent named in the demand may sign even if no separate POA has been filed with any office (Rules 90.1(c),(d),90.3(b),90.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and signature rules for additional or sub‑agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment of an additional or sub-agent can be made in the demand or through a separate/general POA. If appointment made in demand signed by applicant, no separate POA required. If the demand is signed by an earlier appointed agent and that agent has the right to appoint sub-agents, no separate POA needed. If the demand is signed by the additional/sub-agent, a separate POA may be required unless IPEA waived the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a separate POA accompanies the demand or is later filed, the IPEA promptly transmits original or copy to the IB. See Rules 90.2(a),(b),90.3(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative may sign for all applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: A common representative is entitled to sign the demand with effect for all applicants; the agent of the common representative may also sign with effect for all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper indication of common representative and associated agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required indications concerning the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must contain prescribed indications concerning the applicant. The address must indicate the country (letter code in postal code acceptable); nationality and residence must be indicated by name or two-letter country codes; for dependent territories indicate the State on which the territory depends. If there are multiple applicants, it is sufficient that one of them who has the right to make a demand provides address, nationality and residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Section 115 for manner of indicating names of States. For right to make demand, see paragraph 22.34 and Section 614.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to make a demand judged at time of filing; corrections permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: For the decision whether the applicant had the right to make a demand, it is decisive that the applicant had the right at the time the demand was filed. Omissions or wrong indications may be corrected by the applicant if the IPEA is satisfied the applicant had the right at the time of receipt; in such case the demand is considered to have met Article 31(2)(a) requirements as of the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA may accept corrections that establish entitlement at the filing date; ensures demand retains original filing date for procedural purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indications concerning the agent — verification and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent is named or appointed, the IPEA checks whether the indications correspond to those in the file. If IPEA has no information about the appointment, it checks publication or PCT Gazette or with IB. For a new agent appointment, the IPEA checks compliance with Rules 4.4 and 4.16 (Rule 4.7 applies mutatis mutandis). The IPEA may waive the requirement for a POA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA may request receiving Office to confirm agent's right to practice (Form PCT/IPEA/410) if agent does not have right to practice before IPEA; follow Rule 90.1(c),(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct defects and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA finds defects referred to in Rule 60.1(a), it invites the applicant to correct them within one month from date of invitation (Form PCT/IPEA/404). A copy of the invitation is sent to the IB. For lack of signature, the IPEA may include the last sheet for the applicant/agent to sign and return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where IPEA waived POA requirement and lack of signature is the defect, agent may sign and return last sheet included with invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling corrections/replacement sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a correction or replacement sheet, the IPEA marks the date received, verifies identity of replacement sheet with the replaced sheet, marks 'SUBSTITUTE SHEET (RULE 60.1)' and keeps copies of any letters and replacement sheets; it transmits replacement sheets and copies of letters to the IB. These actions apply even if corrections are untimely and demand is later considered as not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow paragraphs 22.38–22.39 and Rules 60.1 and 60.1(c) for marking and transmission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary unsolicited corrections treated similarly
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submits a replacement sheet voluntarily without invitation, the IPEA proceeds as with invited corrections (marks, verifies, transmits, keeps copies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle unsolicited corrections transparently and notify IB as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of corrections and extension of time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant complies within the time limit, the demand is considered as received on the actual filing date provided the demand permitted identification. The time limit for correction may be extended; if correction is received after expiration but before decision, the time limit should be extended ex officio so correction is considered timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Rule 60.1(a),(b) and extend ex officio where appropriate to avoid penalizing late-but-received-before-decision corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration that demand is considered not submitted for uncorrected defects
rubrics_metrics.description: If defects referred to in Rule 60.1(a) have not been corrected or not timely corrected, the IPEA declares the demand to be considered as if it had not been submitted and notifies applicant and the IB (Form PCT/IPEA/407). If the date of receipt of the demand is changed, the IPEA notifies using Form PCT/IPEA/402.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate forms and ensure parties are notified promptly when a demand is considered not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation, determination and notification of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA calculates amounts of the prescribed preliminary examination fee and handling fee, determines whether fees have been paid and notifies the applicant of any underpayment or overpayment (optionally using Form PCT/IPEA/403).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling fee amount set in Schedule of Fees; preliminary examination fee amount fixed by the IPEA (Rules 57, 58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for payment of handling and preliminary examination fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The handling fee and preliminary examination fee are payable within one month from date the demand was submitted or 22 months from priority date, whichever expires later. If demand transmitted under Rule 59.3, fees payable within one month from actual receipt by that Authority or 22 months from priority date, whichever later. If IPEA starts international preliminary examination at same time as search, it invites payment within one month from date of invitation; amount payable is that applicable on date of payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees unpaid or insufficient before due date, IPEA may invite applicant to pay missing amount (Form PCT/IPEA/403).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment fee and consequences of non‑payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a late payment fee is charged, its amount is 50% of the amount of unpaid fees specified in the invitation, or, if that is less than the handling fee, an amount equal to the handling fee may be charged. The late payment fee must not exceed double the amount of the handling fee. If applicant does not pay missing amount (including late fee) within one month of invitation, IPEA declares demand considered not submitted (Form PCT/IPEA/407). If amount received before declaration, payment is considered timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Rules 58bis.1 and 58bis.2 and Rules 54.4,57.4 for treatment of late payments and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of handling fee in certain circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA refunds the handling fee to the applicant if the demand is withdrawn before it has been sent to the IB or considered not to have been submitted because none of the applicants had the right to make a demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process refunds as appropriate where demand not processed or invalid because of entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly transfer of handling fees to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA should, each month, transfer the handling fees collected during the preceding month to the IB, indicating exact amounts transferred, broken down by international application numbers and applicant names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear breakdown to IB to ensure correct allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for original confirmation of faxed/telecommunicated documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original of a document is required as confirmation of a document transmitted by facsimile, telegraph, teleprinter or other means, and the original signed document is not received within 14 days, an invitation is sent to the applicant to comply within a reasonable time (optionally using Form PCT/ISA/230 or PCT/IPEA/434). The original need not be submitted unless required by the Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to comply within the time limit, Authority notifies the applicant that the document is considered not to have been submitted (Form PCT/ISA/232 or PCT/IPEA/438).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of paper submissions by authorities requiring electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Authority only accepts submissions in electronic form, it treats any documents submitted on paper as not received and promptly notifies the applicant accordingly (Form PCT/ISA/231 or PCT/IPEA/435). The Authority may, in a particular case, accept documents submitted via other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities should notify applicants promptly and may exercise discretion to accept paper in exceptional cases (see Rules 89bis.1(d-bis) and 89bis.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic resubmission requirement for paper documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Authority requires electronic resubmission of documents submitted on paper, it invites the applicant to make the electronic submission (Form PCT/ISA/230 or PCT/IPEA/434). If applicant fails to respond timely, the Authority disregards the paper document and notifies the applicant (Form PCT/ISA/232 or PCT/IPEA/438). Alternatively the Authority may convert the paper document into electronic form in accordance with Section 705bis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rules 89bis.1(d-ter) and 89bis.2 and conversion procedures where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency between original text and electronic resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority notices any inconsistency between the original text and the electronic resubmission before the expiration of the applicable two-month time limit, it should draw the applicant's attention to the inconsistency and give an opportunity to correct before the expiration of the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide applicant with chance to resolve inconsistencies prior to deadline to avoid loss of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in mail service — reliance on Rule 82
rubrics_metrics.description: For delays, loss in the mail or interruption in mail service, reference is made to Rule 82. Rule 82 applies also if a delivery service is used to the extent that the Authority accepts evidence of mailing by that delivery service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess evidence of mailing from delivery services if accepted by the Authority; follow Rule 82 procedures for proof and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse of delay in meeting time limits (Rule 82quater.1 conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay in meeting a time limit is to be excused under Rule 82quater.1 if the Authority is satisfied that: (a) the time limit was not met due to war, revolution, civil disorder, strike, natural calamity, epidemic, general unavailability of electronic communication services or other like reason in the locality where the interested party resides/has business/is staying; (b) the relevant action was taken as soon as reasonably possible; (c) the evidence provided is in a form acceptable to the Authority (or waiver applies); and (d) the evidence or statement is received by the Authority not later than six months after expiration of the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable evidence: reliable news report, statement/announcement from national authority, ISP or electricity provider statement in case of electronic outage. Authorities judge 'as soon as reasonably possible' on facts (examples given). In exceptional circumstances, Authority may waive requirement for evidence and publish conditions for such waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse for unavailability of electronic means at the Authority (Rule 82quater.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 82quater.2 allows the ISA, Authority for supplementary search, or IPEA to provide for excuse of delay due to unavailability of permitted electronic means of communication at the Authority; if Authority provides for such excuse it notifies the IB which will publish in the Gazette and the Authority publishes details of unavailability including period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such an event occurs or is scheduled (e.g., maintenance), Authority should publish and notify IB so Gazette entry can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for excusing delay due to Authority electronic unavailability (Rule 82quater.2 operational tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Authority provides an excuse under Rule 82quater.2, it excuses delay if: (a) the applicant indicates, where required, that the time limit was not met due to unavailability of permitted electronic means at the Authority; (b) the Authority acknowledges that such means were not available during the period concerned; and (c) the relevant action was performed on the next working day on which such means became available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate outage where required; Authorities must acknowledge outage and confirm next‑working‑day action to excuse delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority notification and transmission related to excuse decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority should promptly inform the interested party of its decision regarding excuse of delay (using Form PCT/ISA/224 or PCT/IPEA/424) and also transmit a copy of the decision and any request and evidence furnished to the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified forms and send copies to IB for Gazette/publication and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits when Authority State experiences general disruption (Rule 82quater.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the State in which the Authority is located experiences a general disruption caused by an event listed in Rule 82quater.1 that affects operations at the Authority and thereby interferes with ability of interested parties to perform actions, the Authority may decide to establish a period of extension in accordance with Rule 82quater.3. The Authority may do so if (1) the State is experiencing a general disruption caused by such an event (need not affect entire State) and (2) the disruption has affected Authority operations and significantly impacted its ability to provide usual services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority should assess whether conditions (1) and (2) are met before establishing an extension period and publish/notify IB as required.
